subject: POC planning: success criteria, timelines & risk tracker - Stellar Commerce
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Peters <john.peters@stellarcommerce.com>, Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@stellarcommerce.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC planning: success criteria & next steps (Stellar Commerce)

Hi John & Emily,

Thanks again for the call today \u0004 great alignment on objectives. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the POC (4-week trial) scheduled and minimize surprises. Please confirm owners and the kickoff date below.

High-level POC goal
- Validate Redwood Inference integration for checkout personalization flows with predictable latency and cost.

Success criteria (proposed)
- Functional: model integration completes end-to-end with your checkout test harness
- Performance: 95th percentile latency < 200ms for checkout traffic at expected QPS (see evaluation plan)
- Stability: no data-loss incidents during test window, graceful degradation under load
- Cost: per-seat inference cost within target (we'll share cost model after sampling)

Evaluation plan & timeline
- Kickoff: week of Sept 14 (propose Sept 15 10:00am PT) 04 technical onboarding and access
- Week 1: baseline integration, smoke tests, sample dataset ingestion
- Week 2: synthetic load tests + latency profiling (we'll run together)
- Week 3: real traffic shadowing (if you\u0019re comfortable) + cost run rate estimate
- Week 4: acceptance testing & handover / next steps

Owners
- Stellar Commerce: Emily Zhao (product), John Peters (SRE) 04 please confirm; add procurement contact for contract timeline
- Redwood: Marissa Cole (AE) and Dev Patel (Solutions Engineer)

Immediate asks
1) Confirm kickoff: Sept 15 OK?
2) Confirm internal owners & procurement contact (Lori Miles?)
3) Share sample payload and any rate limits we should honor
4) Confirm whether you need SOC 2 / data residency docs up front

I've attached the initial SOW draft and a working POC risk tracker (spreadsheet) for us to populate. I'll update the tracker as we confirm owners and known risks.

Attachments: POC-Risk-Tracker.xlsx, SOW-draft-v2.pdf

Thanks 04 looking forward to kicking this off.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: John Peters <john.peters@stellarcommerce.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@stellarcommerce.com>
Cc: Lori Miles <lori.miles@stellarcommerce.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC planning: success criteria & next steps (Stellar Commerce)

Marissa 04 thanks for the recap. A few notes / clarifications from our side:

- Confirmed owners: Emily (product), myself (SRE) and I'll add Samir Khan (our infra lead) to technical threads. Procurement will be Lori Miles (cc'd).
- SOC 2 / compliance: we will need SOC 2 Type II report and a short summary of data handling during the POC (especially around logs and KV cache). Can you share now?
- Latency target: we agree the 95th pctl target is the right metric; can you confirm 95th <200ms applies to the checkout request path specifically? We'll want to test the end-to-end flow with our checkout QA harness.
- Timeline: Sept 14 is tight for several of our folks; can we move kickoff to Sept 15 (10am PT) instead?

Also, a question about mitigations: if we see latency spikes during synthetic load, do you have recommended short-term mitigations (reduced batch sizes, fallback model, etc.) to keep checkout healthy while you triage?

I'll start lining up the sample payloads and will share them by end of day today.

Thanks,
John
SRE Lead, Stellar Commerce
john.peters@stellarcommerce.com

Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC planning: success criteria & next steps (Stellar Commerce)

John 04 perfect, thanks for the quick responses and for adding the procurement/tech contacts. Updated notes below and a couple of items we committed to provide:

- Kickoff: Sept 15 10:00am PT 04 updated on our side and invites to follow.
- Success criteria: yes 04 95th pctl <200ms for the checkout request path. We'll document the exact request shape for testing in the evaluation plan.
- SOC 2: link to report and summary here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1SOC2-report 04 we will also provide a one-page summary of data handling for the POC (logs, retention, encryption at rest/in transit).
- Short-term mitigations: yes 04 recommended fallbacks are (1) reduce batch_size to 1, (2) route to a lower-capacity variant with smaller KV state, or (3) short-circuit to a cached default response for non-critical requests. We'll walk through feasibility on the kickoff call.

I've attached an updated SOW (v2 updated for procurement) and a populated POC-Risk-Tracker.xlsx with initial risks and owners. Please review the tracker; I've added lines for SOC 2 evidence, data access, and latency mitigation.

Attachments: SOW-draft-v2-updated.pdf, POC-Risk-Tracker.xlsx

Looking forward to the kickoff 04 invite with dial-in and pre-work will hit your calendars shortly.

Best,
Marissa

From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@stellarcommerce.com>

Cc: John Peters <john.peters@stellarcommerce.com>, Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@stellarcommerce.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC planning: success criteria & next steps (Stellar Commerce)

Marissa / Dev 04 quick heads up from our preliminary SDK integration work: we reproduced a hard error when sending batched requests to the Redwood SDK (error id: XZY-301). The stacktrace suggests a header parsing issue inside the client when multiple recipients are present. Repro steps attached.

This is blocking our ability to run the synthetic load tests 04 temporarily marking as priority-blocker in our internal tracker. Can your engineering team triage? In the meantime, is there a recommended workaround (e.g., set batch_size to 1) we should use to unblock testing?

I've attached logs and screenshots: error-screenshots.zip

Regards,
Samir
Infra Lead, Stellar Commerce

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@stellarcommerce.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, John Peters <john.peters@stellarcommerce.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC planning: success criteria & next steps (Stellar Commerce)

Samir 04 thanks for the debug info and attached logs. Quick triage update:

- Root cause: client SDK v1.2 has an edge-case in header serialization when sending batched payloads with multiple recipients; this causes a malformed header and the server rejects the request (error XZY-301).
- Short-term mitigation (do this now): set batch_size = 1 in your client configuration. That will avoid the batched header path and unblock load testing.
- Hotfix plan: we will release a patch to the SDK (v1.2.1) that fixes header serialization. Target deploy: Sept 12, 10:00am PT. We will run canary on a small subset and monitor for regressions.
- Rollback / escalation: if the patch causes regressions, we'll revert to v1.2 and follow the mitigation above. For urgent escalation, contact on-call: oncall@redwood.ai or Dev Patel (dev.patel@redwood.ai / +1 (415) 555-0167).

I've updated the POC-Risk-Tracker.xlsx to mark this as a priority-blocker with owner Michael Grant and mitigation steps. Ticket: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/RI-9876

Please confirm you can switch to batch_size=1 for now and we'll coordinate the patch window.

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Senior Software Engineer, Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.ai
